title: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
slides: Could a copyright ruling kill Wikipedia's open web?
Wikimedia warns courts may treat AI training as infringement
But the real target is not AI, it's fair use itself
Your reuse of public knowledge could face new licensing fees
Ask your legal team: does scraping still count as fair use?
thread_text:
1. Copyright vs. Wikipedia

Wikimedia warns courts may treat AI training as infringement — but the real target isn't AI, it's fair use itself.

2. The real target

If training AI on public data becomes infringement, your reuse of public knowledge could face new licensing fees.

3. Your reuse at risk

Fair use has long protected scraping and indexing. A ruling against it would affect far more than Wikipedia.

4. The open web at stake

A copyright ruling could kill the open web by making everyday reuse of public information legally risky.

5. Ask your legal team

Does scraping still count as fair use in your workflow? Check your data practices before the next ruling drops.

instagram.caption:
A court could soon decide that training AI on public data counts as copyright infringement — and Wikimedia says that ruling could hit far more than Wikipedia. ⚖️

The real target isn't AI. It's fair use, the doctrine that has long let people scrape and index public information without paying.

If that flips, everyday reuse of public knowledge could come with new licensing fees. 📉

That means your own workflow — research, archiving, building tools on public data — might suddenly carry legal risk.

Does scraping still count as fair use in what you do? Ask your legal team before the next ruling drops. 🗂️
